svg.title: What the harness can prove about a change
svg.desc: One task's evidence chain from spec to receipt, tied together by a spec fingerprint and a code fingerprint; the places it is checked again outside the agent's session; and shipped evidence extensions under accepted ADRs, with further work pending.
svg.text: What the harness can prove about a change
One task's evidence chain, where it is checked again, and the shipped extensions of accepted ADRs
ONE TASK'S CHAIN · IN BACKBONE/ AND GIT
Edit the spec or an ADR and the grill, judge and review passes go stale; change any code and the judge and review passes do.
Gates re-derive a stored pass from its evidence, so a hand-written pass doesn't count. Verdict history is append-only, and agents' writes to it are refused.
CHECKED AGAIN, OUTSIDE THE AGENT'S SESSION

g.data-component-ids: ADR-003 · in the judge pass and receipt
g.text: ADR-003 · IN THE JUDGE PASS AND RECEIPT
Each judge pass records where it ran: backend, isolation class, base

g.data-component-ids: ADR-004 · read from backbone/ and git
g.text: ADR-004 · READ FROM BACKBONE/ AND GIT
trace export --format reqif | reqifz | needs | html: requirement → AC
→ test → verdict → commit. Derived and one-way; no gate reads it
attest --range: an in-toto statement about a commit and its code
tree, only for a range that verifies. On a push to main, CI writes it
with the previous tip's engine and signs it: with a key that matches
harness-attest.pub, a cloud KMS key, or keyless when opted in.

svg.text: A record in backbone/ or git
Checked again by the harness or CI
A shipped slice of an accepted ADR
Sources: backbone/HOOKS.md (change receipt, verify, traceability export, signed verdict attestation), ADR-003, ADR-004 and ADR-005 at v0.32.0.
An accepted ADR's shipped slice is solid; it does not mean every follow-up of that ADR is built.
